48676.q: Which big city is on Lake Michigan?
48676.e: Chicago is one of the biggest cities in the USA. It lies on the south-west shore of Lake Michigan.

48677.q: Which big city in Canada is on Lake Ontario?
48677.e: Toronto is the biggest city in Canada. It lies on the north shore of Lake Ontario.

48678.q: Which river carries the water of the Great Lakes to the Atlantic?
48678.e: The water flows from Lake Ontario into the St Lawrence River. This flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
48678.m: The St Lawrence River links the Great Lakes with the Atlantic.

48679.q: Which of these lakes is one of the Great Lakes?
48679.e: Lake Huron is one of the five Great Lakes in North America. Lake Constance is in Europe.
48679.m: Lake Huron is one of the Great Lakes.

48680.q: Which whale with a long tusk lives in the seas around Greenland?
48680.e: The narwhal lives in the icy sea of the Arctic. In the male, one tooth grows into a long, twisted tusk.
48680.m: The narwhal has a long tusk.

48681.e: A thick ice sheet covers about four fifths of the island. There is ice-free land only along the coast.
48681.m: Most of Greenland lies under ice.

48682.q: Which country does Greenland belong to?
48682.e: Greenland is part of the Kingdom of Denmark. But it runs many of its own affairs.
48682.m: Greenland belongs to the Kingdom of Denmark.

48683.q: What is the capital of Greenland?
48683.e: Nuuk lies on the west coast of Greenland. It is the largest town on the island.
48683.m: The capital of Greenland is Nuuk.

48684.q: What can you experience in northern Greenland in summer?
48684.e: In summer in the far north, the sun stays in the sky day and night. This is called the midnight sun.
48684.m: In summer there is the midnight sun in northern Greenland.

48685.q: What breaks off the glaciers on Greenland’s coast and drifts out to sea?
48685.e: The glaciers push their ice right into the sea. There, big pieces break off and float away as icebergs.

48686.e: The Viking Erik the Red called the island ‘Green land’. He wanted the nice name to attract settlers.

48687.q: About how many times bigger than Switzerland is Greenland?
48687.e: Greenland covers more than 2 million square kilometres. Switzerland has about 41,000 square kilometres, so it fits in more than 50 times.
48687.m: Greenland is more than 50 times as big as Switzerland.

48688.q: Looking at the map, which continent does Greenland belong to?
48688.e: Greenland lies north-east of Canada. That is why it counts as part of North America geographically.
48688.m: Geographically, Greenland is in North America.

48689.q: Which cat-like predator lives only on Madagascar?
48689.e: The fossa looks a bit like a cat with a long tail. It climbs well and also hunts animals in the trees.
48689.m: The fossa is a predator that lives only on Madagascar.

48690.q: Which food is eaten with almost every meal on Madagascar?
48690.e: People on Madagascar eat a lot of rice, often even three times a day. Rice is grown in many fields on the island.
48690.m: People on Madagascar eat a lot of rice.

48691.q: Which big-eyed animals live in the wild almost only on Madagascar?
48691.e: Lemurs are relatives of monkeys with long tails. In the wild they live only on Madagascar and the nearby Comoros.

48692.q: What is the name of the tree with a very thick trunk that grows on Madagascar?
48692.e: The baobab is also called the monkey-bread tree. It stores a lot of water in its thick trunk.
48692.m: Baobabs with thick trunks grow on Madagascar.

48693.q: Which animals can change colour and live in large numbers on Madagascar?
48693.e: About half of all chameleon species live on Madagascar. They can change their colour.
48693.m: Especially many chameleons live on Madagascar.

48694.q: Which spice is grown in particularly large amounts on Madagascar?
48694.e: Madagascar is one of the most important countries for vanilla. A lot of the vanilla for ice cream and cakes comes from there.
48694.m: A lot of vanilla comes from Madagascar.

48695.q: What is the capital of Madagascar?
48695.e: Antananarivo lies in the highlands in the middle of the island. It is the largest city in Madagascar.
48695.m: The capital of Madagascar is Antananarivo.

48696.q: Where does Madagascar rank among the largest islands in the world?
48696.e: Only Greenland, New Guinea and Borneo are bigger. That makes Madagascar the fourth largest island in the world.
48696.m: Madagascar is the fourth largest island in the world.

48697.q: Besides Malagasy, which language is an official language on Madagascar?
48697.e: Madagascar used to be a French colony. That is why French is still an official language there today.
48697.m: On Madagascar people speak Malagasy and French.

48698.q: Which giant animals are the Galápagos Islands famous for?
48698.e: Tortoises weighing more than 200 kilograms live on the islands. They can live to a very great age.
48698.m: Giant tortoises live on the Galápagos Islands.

48699.q: Which famous scientist visited the Galápagos Islands in 1835?
48699.e: Charles Darwin observed many animals on the islands. This later helped him with his theory of how species develop.
48699.m: Charles Darwin explored the Galápagos Islands.

48700.q: Which lizard on the Galápagos Islands dives in the sea for seaweed?
48700.e: The marine iguana is the only lizard that swims and dives in the sea. It eats algae off the rocks.
48700.m: The marine iguana dives in the sea for algae.

48701.q: Which birds, usually known from cool places, live on the Galápagos Islands?
48701.e: The Galápagos penguin lives there even though the sun is hot. Cool sea water from the south brings it enough fish.
48701.m: Penguins live on the Galápagos Islands.

48702.q: How were the Galápagos Islands formed?
48702.e: The islands are the tops of volcanoes that rise out of the sea. Some of the volcanoes still erupt today.
48702.m: The Galápagos Islands were formed by volcanoes.

48703.q: Which imaginary line runs through the Galápagos Islands?
48703.e: The equator divides the Earth into a northern and a southern half. It runs right through the group of islands.
48703.m: The equator runs through the Galápagos Islands.

48704.q: Which small birds on the Galápagos Islands have differently shaped beaks depending on the island?
48704.e: These finches have beaks that suit their food. They helped a famous scientist understand how species develop.
48704.m: Special finches with different beaks live on the Galápagos Islands.

48705.q: In which ocean are the Maldives?
48705.e: The Maldives lie in the Indian Ocean. The water there is warm all year round.
48705.m: The Maldives are in the Indian Ocean.

48706.q: Roughly how many islands make up the Maldives?
48706.e: The Maldives are made up of about 1,200 small islands. People live on only about 200 of them.

48707.q: What is the capital of the Maldives?
48707.e: Malé is a small island almost completely covered with buildings. A large part of the population lives there.
48707.m: The capital of the Maldives is Malé.

48708.q: Which country is considered the flattest country in the world?
48708.e: The islands of the Maldives mostly rise only one or two metres out of the sea. No other country is so flat.
48708.m: The Maldives are the flattest country in the world.

48709.q: What are the islands of the Maldives made of?
48709.e: The islands formed from coral reefs and coral sand. That is why the beaches there are so white.
48709.m: The Maldives are made of coral.

48710.q: Why are the Maldives in danger in the future?
48710.e: If the sea rises higher, the flat islands may be flooded. This threatens people’s homes.
48710.m: A rising sea level threatens the Maldives.

48711.q: What do you call a ring-shaped coral island like those in the Maldives?
48711.e: An atoll is a ring of coral reefs and islands. In the middle there is a shallow lagoon.
48711.m: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral island.

48712.q: The Maldives are the smallest country of which continent?
48712.e: The Maldives count as part of Asia. No other country in Asia has so little land.
48712.m: The Maldives are the smallest country in Asia.

48713.q: Which large country are the Maldives near?
48713.e: The Maldives lie south-west of the southern tip of India. Sri Lanka is not far away either.
48713.m: The Maldives lie south-west of India.

48714.q: What do you call many islands that lie close together in the sea?
48714.e: When many islands lie close together, they are called a group of islands. Another word for it is archipelago.
48714.m: Many islands close together form a group of islands.

48715.q: What do you call a country made up only of islands?
48715.e: An island nation lies entirely on one or more islands. Switzerland, on the other hand, is a landlocked country without a sea.
48715.m: A country made only of islands is called an island nation.

48716.q: Which country do the Azores belong to?
48716.e: The Azores lie in the middle of the Atlantic. They belong to Portugal.

48717.q: Which country in Asia is made up of four large main islands and many small ones?
48717.e: Japan’s four large islands are called Honshu, Hokkaido, Kyushu and Shikoku. There are also thousands of small islands.
48717.m: Japan is made up of four large main islands.

48718.q: Which country do the Canary Islands belong to?
48718.e: The Canary Islands lie in the Atlantic off Africa. They belong to Spain.
48718.m: The Canary Islands belong to Spain.

48719.q: Which country do the Cyclades belong to?
48719.e: The Cyclades lie in the Aegean Sea in the Mediterranean. Well-known islands are Naxos and Santorini.

48720.q: Which group of islands does Majorca belong to?
48720.e: Majorca is the largest of the Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean. The Balearic Islands belong to Spain.
48720.m: Majorca is one of the Balearic Islands.

48721.q: Which country is made up of two large main islands in the Pacific?
48721.e: New Zealand is made up of the North Island and the South Island. There are also many smaller islands.
48721.m: New Zealand has a North Island and a South Island.

48722.q: Which group of islands lies in Lake Maggiore in Ticino?
48722.e: The Brissago Islands are two small islands in Lake Maggiore. On the larger one there is a garden with plants from all over the world.
48722.m: The Brissago Islands are in Lake Maggiore.

48723.q: Which country do the Faroe Islands belong to?
48723.e: The Faroe Islands lie in the North Atlantic between Scotland and Iceland. They belong to the Kingdom of Denmark.
48723.m: The Faroe Islands belong to the Kingdom of Denmark.

a: Land with water on three sides
Land with water on all sides
A mountain in the middle of the sea
A lake in the middle of the land
48724.e: A peninsula sticks out into the water. Only on one side is it joined to the rest of the land.
48724.m: A peninsula is surrounded by water on three sides.

48725.q: Which country lies on a peninsula shaped like a boot?
48725.e: Italy sticks out into the Mediterranean. On the map it looks like a boot.
48725.m: Italy is shaped like a boot.

48726.q: Which two countries lie on the Iberian Peninsula?
48726.e: The Iberian Peninsula lies in south-west Europe. Spain and Portugal share almost all of it.
48726.m: Spain and Portugal lie on the Iberian Peninsula.

48727.q: Which is the largest peninsula in the world?
48727.e: The Arabian Peninsula lies in Asia between the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf. No peninsula is bigger.
48727.m: The Arabian Peninsula is the largest peninsula in the world.

48728.q: Which US state is a peninsula in the south?
48728.e: Florida sticks far out into the sea in the south-east of the USA. It is surrounded by water on three sides.
48728.m: Florida is a peninsula in the south of the USA.

48729.q: On which peninsula do Norway and Sweden lie?
48729.e: The Scandinavian Peninsula lies in the north of Europe. Norway and Sweden share it.
48729.m: Norway and Sweden lie on the Scandinavian Peninsula.

48730.q: Which country lies mostly on the Jutland peninsula?
48730.e: Jutland sticks out northwards into the sea from Germany. Most of it belongs to Denmark.
48730.m: Most of Jutland belongs to Denmark.

48731.q: On which peninsula in northern Europe do Norway and Sweden lie?
48731.e: Norway and Sweden share the Scandinavian Peninsula. It is the largest peninsula in Europe.
48731.m: Norway and Sweden lie on the Scandinavian Peninsula.

48732.q: On which peninsula does Greece lie?
48732.e: Greece lies in the south of the Balkan Peninsula. Many islands in the Mediterranean belong to it too.
48732.m: Greece lies on the Balkan Peninsula.

48733.q: What does the wind from the Sahara sometimes carry all the way to Switzerland?
48733.e: Strong winds carry fine Sahara dust across the Mediterranean to us. Then the sky turns yellowish and the snow in the Alps sometimes turns reddish.
48733.m: Sahara dust can fly all the way to Switzerland.

48734.q: On which continent is the Sahara?
48734.e: The Sahara covers a large part of North Africa. It stretches from the Atlantic to the Red Sea.
48734.m: The Sahara is in the north of Africa.

48735.q: What does the Arabic word ‘Sahara’ mean?
48735.e: ‘Sahara’ comes from Arabic and simply means ‘desert’. So the name really means ‘the desert’.
48735.m: The word Sahara means desert in Arabic.

48736.q: What is most of the Sahara made of?
48736.e: Only about one fifth of the Sahara is covered with sand dunes. The rest is rock, stones and gravel.
48736.m: The Sahara is mainly stones and rock, not just sand.

48737.q: Which small fox with very big ears lives in the Sahara?
48737.e: The desert fox is also called the fennec. It loses heat through its big ears and hears prey in the sand.
48737.m: The desert fox has huge ears to cope with the heat.

48738.q: Which people have travelled through the Sahara with camels for a long time?
48738.e: The Tuareg live in the Sahara. The men often wear a long face veil against the sun and sand.
48738.m: The Tuareg are a desert people of the Sahara.

48739.q: Which of these countries has part of the Sahara?
48739.e: Algeria is in North Africa. A very large part of the country is Sahara.
48739.m: Algeria is a country with a lot of Sahara.

48740.q: Is the Sahara bigger or smaller than Switzerland?
48740.e: The Sahara is more than 200 times as big as Switzerland. It measures about 9 million square kilometres.
48740.m: Switzerland would fit into the Sahara more than 200 times.

48741.q: Which desert is even bigger than the Sahara?
48741.e: Antarctica also counts as a desert because it gets very little precipitation. It is a cold desert and bigger than the Sahara.
48741.m: The largest desert in the world is cold Antarctica.

48742.q: On which continent is the Gobi Desert?
48742.e: The Gobi lies in Central Asia. It is one of the largest deserts in the world.
48742.m: The Gobi Desert is in Asia.

48743.q: In which two countries is the Gobi Desert?
48743.e: The Gobi lies in the south of Mongolia and in the north of China.
48743.m: The Gobi is in Mongolia and China.

48744.q: What is winter like in the Gobi Desert?
48744.e: In winter it can get colder than minus 30 degrees in the Gobi. Sometimes there is even snow.
48744.m: Winters in the Gobi are icy cold.

48745.q: What famous find did scientists make in the Gobi Desert?
48745.e: Fossilised dinosaur eggs were discovered in the Gobi in the 1920s. Many fossils are still found there today.
48745.m: The Gobi is known for dinosaur finds.

48746.q: Which camel with two humps lives in the Gobi?
48746.e: The Bactrian camel has two humps and a thick winter coat. This helps it survive the cold of the Gobi.
48746.m: The two-humped Bactrian camel lives in the Gobi.

48747.q: What are the round tents that many nomads in the Gobi live in called?
48747.e: A yurt is a round tent with thick felt walls. The nomads can take it down and bring it along when they move on with their animals.
48747.m: Many nomads in the Gobi live in yurts.

48748.q: What stops the rain clouds, so that little rain falls in the Gobi?
48748.e: To the south lie the Tibetan Plateau and the Himalayas. The rain clouds from the sea drop their rain before them and hardly reach the Gobi.
48748.m: High mountains keep the rain away from the Gobi.

48749.q: In which country is most of the Atacama Desert?
48749.e: The Atacama lies in the north of Chile in South America. A small part reaches into Peru.
48749.m: The Atacama Desert is mainly in Chile.

48750.q: What is the Atacama Desert especially known for?
48750.e: The Atacama is considered the driest desert outside the polar regions. It almost never rains there.
48750.m: The Atacama is one of the driest places on Earth.

48751.q: Between which sea and which mountain range does the Atacama lie?
48751.e: To the west lies the Pacific Ocean, to the east the high Andes. Both keep the rain away.
48751.m: The Atacama lies between the Pacific and the Andes.

48752.q: Why are there many large telescopes in the Atacama?
a: There is a lot of fog
48752.e: Because the air is so dry, there are hardly any clouds. So you can see the stars especially well.
48752.m: In the Atacama you can see the stars especially clearly.

48753.q: What happens in the Atacama after a rare rainfall?
48753.e: After rain, seeds that have waited in the ground for a long time sprout. This is called the ‘flowering desert’.
48753.m: After rain the Atacama can be full of flowers.

48754.q: Which planet is the Atacama often compared with?
48754.e: The ground is red, stony and very dry, like on Mars. That is why scientists test Mars rovers there.
48754.m: In some places the Atacama looks like Mars.

48755.q: What do you often find as white patches on the ground in the Atacama?
48755.e: In the Atacama there are large salt lakes and salt flats. The water has evaporated and the salt has stayed behind.
48755.m: In the Atacama there are wide white salt flats.

48756.q: In which part of Africa is the Kalahari?
a: In the east by the sea
In the middle on the equator
48756.e: The Kalahari lies in southern Africa. It stretches across several countries.
48756.m: The Kalahari is in the south of Africa.

48757.q: In which country is a large part of the Kalahari?
48757.e: A large part of Botswana is Kalahari. It also reaches into Namibia and South Africa.
48757.m: The Kalahari covers a large part of Botswana.

48758.q: Which small animal often stands upright on guard in the Kalahari?
48758.e: Meerkats live in groups in the Kalahari. One stands on its hind legs and looks out for enemies.
48758.m: In the Kalahari, meerkats stand upright on guard.

48759.q: What colour is the sand in many parts of the Kalahari?
48759.e: In many parts of the Kalahari the sand is reddish. The dunes glow red, especially in the evening.
48759.m: The Kalahari often has red sand.

48760.q: Which people have lived in the Kalahari for a very long time?
48760.e: The San are one of the oldest peoples of Africa. They know the desert very well and used to live as hunter-gatherers.
48760.m: The San have lived in the Kalahari for a long time.

48761.q: What grows in the Kalahari more than in many other deserts?
48761.e: The Kalahari gets a bit more rain than the Sahara. That is why grass, bushes and a few trees grow there.
48761.m: The Kalahari is a desert with lots of grass and bushes.

48762.q: The Kalahari is a desert in Africa. Which big cat hunts there?
48762.e: Lions live in the Kalahari. They can go a long time without drinking and also get liquid from their prey.

48763.q: On which continent are the great deserts of the Arabian Peninsula?
48763.e: The Arabian Peninsula lies in Western Asia. Almost the whole peninsula is desert.
48763.m: The deserts of the Arabian Peninsula are in Asia.

48764.q: Which country has most of the deserts on the Arabian Peninsula?
48764.e: Saudi Arabia is the largest country on the Arabian Peninsula. Most of the country is desert.

48765.q: What do you see almost everywhere in the great sand desert of Arabia?
48765.e: In the great sand desert of Arabia, dune follows dune. It is one of the largest sand deserts in the world.
48765.m: There are huge sand dunes in the desert of Arabia.

48766.q: Why do almost no people live in the great sand desert of Arabia?
48766.e: In the sand desert it is very hot and it almost never rains. Without water, people can hardly live there.
48766.m: There is hardly any water in the desert.

48767.q: Which valuable substance was found under the deserts of the Arabian Peninsula?
48767.e: Huge amounts of oil lie under the desert sand. It has made countries like Saudi Arabia rich.
48767.m: There is a lot of oil under the Arabian desert.

48768.q: Which white antelope with long, straight horns lives in the deserts of Arabia?
48768.e: The Arabian oryx had completely disappeared from the wild. Thanks to protection programmes, it lives free in the desert again today.
48768.m: The Arabian oryx is a white desert antelope.

48769.q: Which one-humped camel is at home on the Arabian Peninsula?
48769.e: The dromedary comes from Arabia. People there have kept it for riding and carrying loads for thousands of years.
48769.m: The one-humped dromedary comes from Arabia.

48770.q: In which country is the Outback?
48770.e: The Outback is the large, dry interior of Australia. Only a few people live there.
48770.m: The Outback is the dry interior of Australia.

48771.q: Which large bird that cannot fly runs through the Outback?
48771.e: After the ostrich, the emu is the largest bird in the world. It cannot fly, but it can run very fast.
48771.m: The emu is a large running bird in the Outback.

48772.q: Which hopping animal lives in the Outback?
48772.e: Kangaroos are at home in Australia. In the Outback you often see them in the evening and the morning.

48773.q: Why is the earth in the Outback often red?
a: Because of iron in the soil
Because of colour from the rain
48773.e: There is a lot of iron in the soil. It rusts and turns the earth red.
48773.m: Rusty iron makes the earth in the Outback red.

48774.q: How do doctors in the Outback often get to sick people?
48774.e: The houses in the Outback are far apart. The ‘flying doctors’ land near the sick people in small planes.
48774.m: In the Outback, doctors fly to sick people by plane.

48775.q: How do many children on remote farms in the Outback learn?
a: With lessons by radio or internet
In a school on every farm
Only with books, without any teacher
By school bus to town every day
48775.e: The nearest school is often hundreds of kilometres away. That is why there is the ‘School of the Air’ with lessons from a distance.
48775.m: Many children in the Outback learn at a school from a distance.

48776.q: Which wild dog lives in the Outback?
48776.e: The dingo is a wild dog in Australia. It is usually yellowish brown.
48776.m: The dingo is Australia’s wild dog.

48777.q: Who has lived in the Outback for a very long time?
48777.e: Aboriginal people are the first inhabitants of Australia. They have lived there for tens of thousands of years.
48777.m: Aboriginal people have lived in Australia for a very long time.

48778.e: A dune is a hill that the wind has piled up out of sand.
48778.m: A dune is a sand hill.

48779.q: Who builds the sand dunes in the desert?
48779.e: The wind carries grains of sand along and drops them in other places. That is how dunes grow.

48780.q: What can dunes do over time?
48780.e: The wind blows sand from one side to the other. In this way the whole dune slowly moves on.
48780.m: Some dunes slowly move across the desert.

48781.q: What shape is a crescent dune?
48781.e: A crescent dune is curved like the crescent moon. Its tips point in the direction the wind is blowing.
48781.m: A crescent dune looks like a half moon.

48782.q: Where in Europe is there a very high sand dune?
48782.e: The Dune du Pilat lies on the Atlantic coast of France. It is about 100 metres high and the highest dune in Europe.
48782.m: The highest dune in Europe is in France on the Atlantic.

48783.q: In which desert in Africa are some of the highest dunes in the world?
48783.e: The Namib lies in Namibia on the Atlantic. Some of its red dunes are more than 300 metres high.
48783.m: The Namib has some of the highest dunes in the world.

48784.q: What can you sometimes hear when sand slides down a dune?
48784.e: When a lot of sand slides, the grains rub against each other. This can make a deep hum; people talk of ‘singing dunes’.
48784.m: Some dunes hum when the sand slides.

48785.q: Apart from the desert, where else are there sand dunes?
48785.e: On the beach too, the wind blows the sand into dunes. There are many dunes on the North Sea, for example.
48785.m: There are also dunes by the sea.

a: A green place with water in the desert
A high mountain in the desert
48786.e: In an oasis there is water. That is why plants grow there and people can live there.
48786.m: An oasis is a green place with water in the desert.

48787.q: Where does the water in many oases come from?
48787.e: In some places there is groundwater under the desert. In an oasis it comes up as a spring or is drawn from wells.
48787.m: The water of an oasis usually comes from the ground.

48788.q: Which trees typically grow in an oasis?
48788.e: Date palms like heat and need water at their roots. Their sweet fruit is important for people in the desert.
48788.m: Many date palms grow in oases.

48789.q: What do you call a group of travellers with many camels?
48789.e: In the past, traders travelled through the desert in long caravans. The camels carried salt, cloth and other goods.
48789.m: A group of travellers with camels is called a caravan.

48790.q: Why did travellers with camels stop at oases in the past?
48790.e: The journey through the desert was long and hot. In the oasis there was water for people and animals.
48790.m: Travellers got water at the oases.

48791.q: What is the name of a famous oasis in Egypt?
48791.e: The Siwa Oasis lies in the desert in the west of Egypt. There are many springs and date palms there.
48791.m: Siwa is a well-known oasis in Egypt.

48792.q: What happens to an oasis when the water in the ground runs out?
48792.e: Without water, the plants can no longer grow. The oasis then turns back into desert.
48792.m: Without water an oasis dries up.

48793.q: What do people grow under the palms in oases?
48793.e: It is cooler in the shade of the palms. There people plant vegetables, grain and herbs.
48793.m: In oases, gardens grow in the shade of the palms.

48794.e: Camels eat grasses, leaves and even thorny and salty plants. The thorns hardly bother their tough mouths.
48794.m: Camels eat plants, even thorny ones.

48795.q: What is stored in a camel’s hump?
48795.e: Many people think the hump contains water. But it is made of fat, which the camel can live on when there is hardly any food.
48795.m: A camel’s hump holds fat, not water.

48796.e: Camels carry people and loads through the desert. When they walk, they sway like a ship.
48796.m: The camel is also called the ship of the desert.

48797.q: What do camels’ long eyelashes help with?
a: Keeping sand out of the eyes
48797.e: The long, thick eyelashes keep sand and dust away from the eyes. That is important in sandstorms.
48797.m: Long eyelashes protect camels’ eyes from sand.

48798.q: What can camels do with their nostrils?
48798.e: Camels can close their nostrils. That way no sand gets in during a sandstorm.
48798.m: Camels can close their noses against sand.

48799.q: Why do camels hardly sink into the sand?
48799.e: Camels have wide, soft soles. Their weight is spread out like with snowshoes.
48799.m: Wide feet carry the camel over the sand.

48800.q: How do camels drink after a long time without water?
48800.e: A thirsty camel drinks a huge amount of water in only about ten minutes. That way it replaces the water it has lost.
48800.m: A thirsty camel drinks a lot at once.

48801.q: In which country do many wild dromedaries live today, even though they are not native there?
48801.e: In the past, people brought dromedaries to Australia as pack animals. Some were set free and now live wild in the Outback.
48801.m: Many wild dromedaries live in Australia.

48803.q: Why do only a few plants grow in the desert?
48803.e: Plants need water to grow. In the desert it rains so rarely that only a few plants survive.
48803.m: Without enough water, only a few plants can grow in the desert.

48804.q: What is a dry riverbed in the desert that only carries water after rain called?
48804.e: A wadi is usually dried up. The word comes from Arabic.
48804.m: A wadi is a desert river that is almost always dry.

48805.q: What can become dangerous in the desert after heavy rain?
48805.e: The hard ground cannot soak up all the water quickly. That is why sudden floods can happen in dry valleys.
48805.m: After heavy rain there can be dangerous floods in the desert.

48806.q: How often does it rain in a desert?
48806.e: In the desert it rains only rarely. Here in Switzerland it rains much more often.
48806.m: In the desert it rains very rarely.

a: Strong wind with lots of sand
48807.e: In a sandstorm the wind whirls lots of sand and dust into the air. Then you often can hardly see anything.
48807.m: In a sandstorm the wind whirls up lots of sand.

48808.q: How long can it sometimes go without raining in a desert?
48808.e: In some deserts no rain falls for years. When it does come, it is often a short shower.
48808.m: In the desert it can stay dry for years.

48809.q: When are many desert animals out and about, to avoid the heat?
48809.e: During the day many animals hide in the shade or in burrows. In the cool night they look for food.
48809.m: Many desert animals are active in the cool night.

48810.q: What is it often like in the Sahara at night?
48810.e: During the day it is hot in the Sahara. But at night the air cools down a lot.
48810.m: Nights in the desert are often cold.

48811.q: Why does it get so cold in the desert at night?
48811.e: Clouds work like a blanket and hold the warmth in. Without clouds, the warmth escapes quickly into the sky at night.
48811.m: Without a blanket of clouds, the desert loses its warmth at night.

48812.q: What can sometimes happen on winter nights in the Sahara?
48812.e: In winter the temperature sometimes drops below zero at night. Then there is a short frost on the ground.
48812.m: There can be frost on winter nights in the Sahara.

48813.q: When is it hottest during the day in the desert?
48813.e: The sun heats the ground and air all morning. That is why it is hottest in the early afternoon.
48813.m: In the desert it is hottest in the early afternoon.

48814.q: Why does the sand in the desert cool down quickly at night?
a: It does not hold heat for long
48814.e: Dry sand gets hot quickly during the day. But it also gives off its heat again quickly at night.
48814.m: Sand gets hot quickly and cold again quickly.

48815.q: Why do many people in the desert wear long, loose clothes?
a: To protect them from the sun
Because it is cold during the day
So that they can be seen from far away
48815.e: Long, loose clothes protect the skin from the strong sun. Underneath, the air stays pleasant.
48815.m: Long clothes protect you from the sun in the desert.

48816.q: What can form in the early morning after a cold desert night?
48816.e: When the air cools down a lot at night, tiny water drops form. Animals and plants use this dew as water.
48816.m: Dew can form on cold desert nights.

48817.q: Where does a cactus store its water?
48817.e: A cactus has a thick, fleshy body. It stores water in it for long, dry periods.
48817.m: A cactus stores water in its thick body.

48818.q: What are a cactus’s spines really?
48818.e: The spines used to be leaves. Because they are so thin, the cactus loses little water.
48818.m: A cactus’s spines are thin, pointed leaves.

48819.q: What else are a cactus’s spines for?
48819.e: Thirsty animals would love to eat the juicy cactus. The sharp spines keep them away.
48819.m: Spines protect the cactus from hungry animals.

48820.q: Which continent do almost all cacti come from?
48820.e: In nature, cacti grow almost only in North and South America. It was people who brought them to Africa and Europe.

48821.q: What is the giant cactus with arms in the Arizona desert called?
48821.e: The saguaro can grow more than 12 metres tall. It grows very slowly and can live for more than 150 years.
48821.m: The saguaro is a giant cactus with arms.

48822.q: How do the roots of many cacti grow?
48822.e: Many cacti have shallow roots that spread out wide. That way they quickly catch even a little rain.
48822.m: Shallow, wide roots help the cactus catch rain.

48823.q: What can you sometimes see on many cacti?
48823.e: Many cacti have large, colourful flowers. Some bloom for only a single night.

48824.q: Why does a cactus have a thick, waxy skin?
48824.e: The thick skin with a layer of wax keeps the water inside the cactus. That way it does not dry out in the sun.
48824.m: The thick skin keeps the water inside the cactus.

48825.e: In a mirage you see things that are not really in that place. It is caused by the air bending light.
48825.m: A Fata Morgana is a mirage.

48826.q: What do people in the desert often think they see in a mirage?
48826.e: A glittering lake seems to lie on the horizon. But there is no water there at all.
48826.m: In a mirage you often see water that is not there.

48827.q: What is often reflected in a desert mirage?
48827.e: The hot air above the ground bends the light from the sky. So the ground looks blue, like water.
48827.m: In a mirage the sky is reflected on the ground.

48828.q: What is needed for a mirage?
48828.e: Above the hot ground, the air is hotter than higher up. There the light gets bent.
48828.m: Hot air above the ground makes a mirage.

48829.q: Where can you see a kind of mirage here in summer too?
48829.e: On hot days a road in the distance sometimes looks wet. That is a mirage too.
48829.m: You can see mirages on hot roads too.

48830.q: What happens if you walk towards a mirage?
48830.e: The water is only a reflection. When you get closer, there is only dry ground.
48830.m: You can never reach a mirage.

48831.q: Can you take a photo of a mirage?
48831.e: A mirage is not something you only imagine. The light really is bent, so a camera can record it.
48831.m: You can even photograph a mirage.

48832.q: Who is the Fata Morgana, a kind of mirage, named after?
48832.e: ‘Fata’ is Italian for ‘fairy’. It means Morgan le Fay from old legends, who could conjure up illusions.
48832.m: The Fata Morgana is named after the fairy Morgana.

48834.q: On which continent is the Amazon rainforest?
48834.e: The Amazon rainforest lies in the north of South America. It covers a large part of the continent.
48834.m: The Amazon rainforest is in South America.

48836.q: What is the giant river in South America where the largest rainforest grows?
48836.e: The Amazon flows through South America. The great rainforest on its banks is named after it.
48836.m: The largest rainforest grows along the Amazon.

48837.q: Which dolphin lives in the Amazon and is often pink?
48837.e: The Amazon river dolphin lives in the fresh water of the rivers. Older animals are often pink.
48837.m: A pink river dolphin lives in the Amazon.

48839.q: Which plant, whose beans are used to make chocolate, comes from the Amazon region?
48839.e: The cacao tree comes from the rainforests of South America. Cocoa and chocolate are made from its beans.
48839.m: The cacao tree originally comes from the Amazon region.

48840.q: How big is the Amazon rainforest compared with Switzerland?
48840.e: The Amazon rainforest covers more than 5 million square kilometres. Switzerland has only just over 41,000 square kilometres.
48840.m: Switzerland would fit into the Amazon rainforest more than a hundred times.

48841.q: Which tree from the Amazon region provides the sap for natural rubber?
48841.e: A milky sap flows from the bark of the rubber tree. Natural rubber is made from it.
48841.m: Natural rubber comes from the rubber tree.

48842.q: On which continent is the Congo rainforest?
48842.e: The Congo rainforest lies in the middle of Africa. It is the largest rainforest on this continent.
48842.m: The Congo rainforest is in the middle of Africa.

48843.q: Where does the Congo rainforest rank among the largest rainforests in the world?
48843.e: Only one rainforest in South America is bigger. That makes the Congo rainforest the second largest.
48843.m: The Congo rainforest is the second largest rainforest on Earth.

48844.q: The Congo rainforest is named after the Congo. What is the Congo?
48844.e: The Congo River flows right through this rainforest. Many smaller rivers flow into it.
48844.m: The Congo rainforest is named after the Congo River.

48845.q: Which great ape lives in the Congo rainforest?
48845.e: Gorillas live only in Africa, among other places in the Congo rainforest. They are the largest great apes.
48845.m: Gorillas live in the rainforests of Africa.

48846.q: The okapi lives in the Congo rainforest. Which animal is it closely related to?
48846.e: The okapi does have stripes on its legs like a zebra. But it is a close relative of the giraffe.
48846.m: The okapi is a relative of the giraffe.

48847.q: Forest elephants live in the Congo rainforest. How do they compare with savannah elephants?
48847.e: Forest elephants are smaller than savannah elephants. That helps them get through the thick forest.
48847.m: Small forest elephants live in the Congo rainforest.

48848.q: Which largest great ape lives in the rainforests of Central Africa, including the Congo Basin?
48848.e: Gorillas live only in Africa, among other places in the Congo rainforest. Orangutans, gibbons and proboscis monkeys live in Asia.
48848.m: Gorillas are the largest great apes and live in Africa.

48849.q: Which country has the largest part of the Congo rainforest?
48849.e: More than half of the Congo rainforest lies in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Neighbouring countries such as Cameroon and Gabon have a share too.
48849.m: Most of the Congo rainforest is in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

48850.e: Borneo is a large island. Much of it is covered with rainforest.
48850.m: Borneo is an island with lots of rainforest.

48851.q: On which continent is the island of Borneo?
48851.e: Borneo lies in South-East Asia. Neighbouring islands include Java and Sulawesi.

48852.q: How many countries share the island of Borneo?
48852.e: On Borneo there are parts of Indonesia and Malaysia, plus the whole of the small country of Brunei. That makes three countries.
48852.m: Three countries share the island of Borneo.

48853.q: Which reddish-brown great ape lives in the rainforest of Borneo?
48853.e: Orangutans live only on Borneo and Sumatra. They have reddish-brown fur and climb skilfully in the trees.

48854.q: Which plant with one of the largest flowers in the world grows on Borneo?
48854.e: The rafflesia has huge flowers without leaves or stems. It smells of rotten meat and attracts flies that way.
48854.m: The rafflesia has huge, smelly flowers.

48855.q: Which bird with a big beak and a casque on top lives on Borneo?
48855.e: Hornbills have a casque on their beak that looks like a horn. They live in Asia and Africa. The toucan looks similar but lives in South America.
48855.m: The hornbill has a horn on its beak.

48856.q: What do pitcher plants on Borneo catch in their pitchers?
48856.e: Pitcher plants have cup-shaped traps with liquid in them. Insects slip in and are digested.
48856.m: Pitcher plants catch insects in their pitchers.

48857.q: Where does Borneo rank among the largest islands in the world?
48857.e: Only Greenland and New Guinea are bigger. Borneo is about 18 times as big as Switzerland.
48857.m: Borneo is the third largest island in the world.

48858.q: What do you call the layer of dense treetops that lies like a roof over the forest?
48858.e: The crowns of the trees grow close together. This makes a green roof high up.
48858.m: The canopy lies like a green roof over the rainforest.

48859.q: What are the single trees that rise even above the canopy called?
48859.e: Emergent trees are especially tall trees. They form the top layer of the rainforest.
48859.m: Emergent trees rise above all the other trees.

48860.q: What is it like on the floor of the rainforest?
48860.e: The dense treetops block out almost all the sunlight. That is why it is gloomy down on the ground.
48860.m: It is dark on the rainforest floor.

48861.q: In which layer of the rainforest do most animals live?
48861.e: In the canopy there is plenty of light, flowers and fruit. That is why most animals live up there.
48861.m: Most rainforest animals live high up in the canopy.

48862.q: Which wide roots support big rainforest trees like walls?
48862.e: Buttress roots grow out from the trunk like tall boards. They hold the tree steady, because the soil is not deep.
48862.m: Buttress roots support the giant trees.

48863.q: What do you call plants like orchids that grow on the branches of trees?
48863.e: Epiphytes grow high up on branches. That way they get more light than on the dark ground.
48863.m: Epiphytes grow on the branches of other trees.

48864.q: How tall can emergent rainforest trees grow?
48864.e: Many emergent trees grow 50 to 70 metres tall. That is as tall as a tower block.
48864.m: Emergent trees can grow taller than 50 metres.

48865.q: Which large bird of prey builds its nest in the tallest trees of the South American rainforest?
48865.e: The harpy eagle is one of the strongest birds of prey in the world. It even hunts monkeys and sloths in the treetops.
48865.m: The harpy eagle is a mighty bird of prey of the rainforest.

48866.q: Which ants cut pieces out of leaves and carry them across the forest floor?
48866.e: Leafcutter ants live in the rainforests of America. They carry the pieces of leaf into their nest and grow a fungus on them, which they eat.
48866.m: Leafcutter ants carry pieces of leaf into their nest.

48867.q: What happens to fallen leaves on the rainforest floor?
48867.e: Warmth and moisture help fungi and small animals. They break down the leaves in a short time.
48867.m: In the warm, damp rainforest, leaves rot very quickly.

48868.q: Near which line on Earth are the tropical rainforests?
48868.e: Tropical rainforests grow around the equator. There the sun shines strongly all year round.
48868.m: Tropical rainforests are near the equator.

48869.q: Where on land do the most different kinds of animals and plants live?
48869.e: No other habitat on land has as many different species as the tropical rainforest. Many of them have not even been discovered yet.
48869.m: Especially many different species live in the tropical rainforest.

48870.q: What does the tropical rainforest not have?
48870.e: In the tropical rainforest it stays warm all year. There is no cold winter like in Switzerland.
48870.m: There is no winter with snow in the tropical rainforest.

48871.q: How often does it rain in the tropical rainforest?
48871.e: It rains very often in the rainforest, often as a heavy shower. That is where the forest gets its name.
48871.m: It rains almost every day in the rainforest.

48872.q: How warm is it usually in the tropical rainforest?
48872.e: The temperature is almost always around 25 degrees. It changes only a little over the year.
48872.m: It is usually around 25 degrees in the rainforest.

48873.q: When are there often heavy downpours in the tropical rainforest?
48873.e: In the morning the sun often shines and a lot of water evaporates. In the afternoon clouds form and it rains heavily.
48873.m: In the rainforest it often rains in the afternoon.

48874.q: What do many leaves in the rainforest have so that rainwater drips off quickly?
48874.e: The leaves end in a long point at the front. The water quickly drips off over this point.
48874.m: With a drip tip, rainwater quickly drips off the leaf.

48875.q: Where does some of the rain in the tropical rainforest come from?
a: From water that plants give off
48875.e: Plants release a lot of water into the air through their leaves. This forms clouds that rain down over the forest.
48875.m: The rainforest makes some of its own rain.

48876.q: What does it mean when the humidity in the rainforest is high?
a: The air contains a lot of water
48876.e: There is a lot of invisible water vapour in the air. That is why the air in the rainforest feels muggy.
48876.m: High humidity means lots of water in the air.

48877.e: Lianas are plants that climb up trees. They do not have a thick trunk of their own to support them.

48878.q: Which way do lianas grow on trees?
48878.e: It is dark on the ground. Lianas climb up the trees until they reach the sun at the top.
48878.m: Lianas climb up towards the light.

48879.q: Where do most lianas have their roots?
48879.e: Most lianas sprout on the forest floor. From there they climb up a tree.
48879.m: Most lianas are rooted in the ground.

48880.q: What do monkeys in the rainforest often use lianas for?
48880.e: Lianas hang between the trees like ropes. Monkeys climb along them and get from tree to tree.
48880.m: Lianas are ropes and bridges for monkeys.

48881.q: How long can some lianas grow?
48881.e: Some lianas grow very long. They can wind more than 100 metres through the forest.
48881.m: Some lianas grow more than 100 metres long.

48882.q: Baskets and furniture are woven from the stems of a climbing palm. What is this material called?
48882.e: The rattan palm climbs up trees like a liana. Rattan furniture is woven from its bendy stems.
48882.m: Rattan comes from a climbing palm.

48883.q: Which spice comes from a climbing orchid?
48883.e: Vanilla is an orchid that climbs up trees. Its pods are used as a spice.
48883.m: Vanilla grows on a climbing plant.

48884.q: Which plant wraps itself around a tree and can crush it over time?
48884.e: The strangler fig often sprouts high up on a tree. Its roots grow downwards and wrap ever more tightly around the tree.
48884.m: The strangler fig can crush a tree.

48885.q: Which climbing plant grows up trees and walls here?
48885.e: Ivy climbs up trees and walls with small clinging roots. It is a liana that also grows here.
48885.m: Ivy is a liana from our woods.

48886.q: What are the large, colourful parrots of South America with long tails called?
48886.e: Macaws include the longest parrots in the world. They live in the rainforests of Central and South America.

48887.q: What are many parrots good at copying?
48887.e: Parrots can imitate sounds. Some even learn words from people.

48888.q: What does a parrot need its strong, curved beak for?
48888.e: The beak is hard and strong like a pair of pliers. Parrots use it to crack nuts and seeds.
48888.m: Parrots crack hard nuts with their beaks.

48889.q: How many toes on a parrot’s foot point forwards?
48889.e: Two toes point forwards and two point backwards. That way parrots can grip branches tightly and hold food.
48889.m: On a parrot, two toes point forwards and two backwards.

48890.q: The African grey parrot has grey feathers and a red tail. On which continent does it live?
48890.e: The African grey lives in Africa, including the Congo rainforest. It is known as an especially good talker.
48890.m: The African grey is a grey parrot from Africa.

48891.q: What is especially striking about the toucan?
48891.e: The toucan has a huge beak. In some species it is almost as long as the body.
48891.m: The toucan has a huge, colourful beak.

48892.q: Where do toucans live in the wild?
48892.e: Toucans live in the forests of Central and South America. There are none in Africa or Asia.

48893.q: How is the toucan’s big beak built?
48893.e: Inside, the beak is built like a sponge with lots of air pockets. That is why it is light despite its size.
48893.m: The toucan’s beak is big but light.

48894.q: What does a toucan mainly eat?
48894.e: Toucans mainly eat fruit. With their long beak they can also reach fruit on thin twigs.

48895.q: What else does the big beak help the toucan to do?
48895.e: A lot of blood flows through the beak. The toucan can lose extra heat through it when it is too hot.
48895.m: The toucan cools itself down through its beak.

48896.e: Sloths move very slowly and save energy that way. It takes them a long time to go a few metres.

48897.q: Where does a sloth spend most of its time?
48897.e: Sloths hang from branches almost all day. They eat, sleep and even have their young in the trees.
48897.m: Sloths usually hang in the trees.

48898.q: About how often does a sloth climb down to the ground to go to the toilet?
48898.e: Sloths digest very slowly. That is why they climb down only about once a week to leave their droppings.
48898.m: Sloths only go to the toilet about once a week.

48899.q: Why does a sloth’s fur often look greenish?
48899.e: Tiny algae grow in the damp fur. The green colour camouflages the sloth among the leaves.

48900.q: What does a sloth mainly eat?
48900.e: Sloths mainly eat leaves. These give only a little energy and are digested slowly.

48901.q: What does a sloth use to hold on to branches?
48901.e: Sloths have long, curved claws like hooks. With them they hang safely from branches, even while asleep.
48901.m: Sloths hang from branches with their hook-like claws.

48902.q: What is a sloth surprisingly good at?
48902.e: On land sloths are very slow. But in water they swim surprisingly well.

48903.q: In which part of the world do sloths live?
48903.e: Sloths live in the rainforests of Central and South America. They are not found in the wild on other continents.
48903.m: Sloths live in Central and South America.

48904.q: Which insects often live in sloths’ fur?
48904.e: Small moths live in the thick fur. They lay their eggs in the droppings when the sloth is on the ground.
48904.m: Small moths live in sloths’ fur.

48905.q: What does the name orangutan mean when translated?
48905.e: The name comes from the Malay language. ‘Orang’ means person and ‘hutan’ means forest.
48905.m: Orangutan means person of the forest.

48906.e: Orangutans have long, reddish-brown to orange hair. That makes them easy to recognise.

48907.q: On which two islands do orangutans live?
48907.e: Wild orangutans are found only on Borneo and Sumatra in South-East Asia. Both islands have large rainforests.
48907.m: Orangutans live only on Borneo and Sumatra.

48908.q: What do orangutans build every evening?
a: A sleeping nest in a tree
48908.e: Orangutans bend branches and leaves together into a nest. They sleep in it high up in the tree.
48908.m: Orangutans sleep in tree nests they build themselves.

48909.q: What do orangutans like to eat most?
48909.e: Orangutans like ripe fruit such as figs best. They also eat leaves, bark and insects.

48910.q: What is especially long on orangutans?
48910.e: Their arms are much longer than their legs. This helps them reach from branch to branch.

48911.q: Which is the largest mammal that lives mainly in trees?
48911.e: Male orangutans can weigh more than 80 kilograms. Even so, they spend most of their time in the trees.
48911.m: The orangutan is the largest tree-dwelling animal.

48912.q: Why are poison dart frogs so colourful?
a: They protect themselves from the sun
So they do not get wet
48912.e: The bright colours tell enemies: watch out, I am poisonous! That is why many animals leave them alone.
48912.m: The bright colours of poison dart frogs are a warning.

48913.q: Where do poison dart frogs have their poison?
48913.e: The poison is in the frogs’ skin. Anyone who eats or licks them can become ill.
48913.m: Poison dart frogs have their poison in their skin.

48914.q: How big are most poison dart frogs?
48914.e: Most poison dart frogs are only about 1.5 to 5 centimetres long. Many are shorter than a thumb.
48914.m: Poison dart frogs are very small frogs.

48915.q: Where do poison dart frogs get their name from?
a: People put their poison on darts
They are as fast as darts
They have darts on their backs
48915.e: Indigenous people in South America coated their hunting darts with the poison of some species. That is where the name comes from.
48915.m: Hunters used to make their darts poisonous with frog poison.

48916.q: Where do poison dart frogs get their poison from?
48916.e: The frogs eat small ants and mites. They make their poison from substances in them.
48916.m: Poison dart frogs get their poison through their food.

48917.q: How do poison dart frogs take their tadpoles to water?
48917.e: The tadpoles stick themselves onto the back of a parent. That way they are carried to a small pool of water.
48917.m: Poison dart frogs carry their tadpoles on their back.

48918.q: On which continent do most poison dart frogs live?
48918.e: Poison dart frogs live in the rainforests of Central and South America. Most species are found in South America.
48918.m: Poison dart frogs live mainly in South America.

48919.q: What happens to the poison when poison dart frogs get different food in a zoo?
48919.e: Without their natural food from the rainforest, they no longer make poison. That is why zoo frogs are usually harmless.
48919.m: In a zoo, poison dart frogs lose their poison.

48920.q: Which frog is one of the most poisonous animals in the world?
48920.e: The golden poison frog lives in Colombia and is often bright yellow. Even a tiny amount of its poison is dangerous.
48920.m: The golden poison frog is extremely poisonous.

48921.e: Every year large areas of rainforest are cut down. As a result, many animals and plants lose their habitat.
48921.m: Deforestation is the biggest danger to the rainforest.

48922.q: Why are many trees cut down in the rainforest?
a: So the animals have more space
48922.e: Many trees are cut down in the rainforest. On the cleared land, fields, pastures and plantations appear, for example for palm oil.
48922.m: A lot of rainforest is cut down for fields and plantations.

48923.q: Which Swiss man from Basel lived for years with a people on Borneo and campaigned for the rainforest?
48923.e: In the 1980s Bruno Manser lived with the Penan in the rainforest of Borneo. He fought against the logging of their forest.
48923.m: Bruno Manser campaigned for the rainforest on Borneo.

48924.q: Where in Switzerland can you visit a rainforest hall with plants and animals from Madagascar?
48924.e: Zurich Zoo has the Masoala Rainforest. The zoo also helps protect Masoala National Park in Madagascar.
48924.m: At Zurich Zoo you can experience a rainforest from Madagascar.

48925.q: What can you do at home to protect forests?
48925.e: Trees are cut down to make paper. If you save paper and use recycled paper, you protect forests.

48926.q: Which gas do the trees in the rainforest take in from the air?
48926.e: Trees take in carbon dioxide and use it to build wood and leaves. That is why the rainforest is important for the climate.
48926.m: Trees take carbon dioxide out of the air.

a: Forest is burnt down for fields
A fire is made for cooking
A forest fire is put out
48927.e: In slash-and-burn, people set fire to the forest. Fields or pastures are then made on the cleared land.
48927.m: In slash-and-burn, forest is burnt down.

48928.q: What do you call a large area where nature and animals are specially protected?
48928.e: In a national park, nature is allowed to develop freely. Switzerland also has a national park in the Engadine.
48928.m: Nature and animals are protected in national parks.

48929.q: What are many forests in the Amazon region cleared for?
48929.e: Large herds of cattle often graze on cleared land. Other areas become soya fields.
48929.m: In the Amazon region, forest is cleared for cattle pastures.

48930.q: How warm is it in the tropics all year round?
48930.e: In the tropics it is warm all year. At midday the sun is very high in the sky there.
48930.m: In the tropics it is warm all year round.

48931.q: Where on Earth are the tropics?
a: Only in the middle of Europe
48931.e: The tropics form a wide belt around the middle of the Earth. That is where the Earth gets the most warmth from the sun.
48931.m: The tropics are in the middle of the Earth.

48932.q: What is the imaginary line that runs through the middle of the tropics called?
48932.e: The equator divides the Earth into a northern and a southern half. It runs through the middle of the tropics.
48932.m: The equator divides the Earth into two halves.

48933.q: Which forest grows in the wet tropics?
48933.e: Where it rains a lot in the tropics, the tropical rainforest grows. A huge number of different animals and plants live there.
48933.m: Especially many animals and plants live in the tropical rainforest.

48934.q: Which colourful bird with a huge beak lives in the South American rainforest?
48934.e: The toucan has a big, colourful beak. It lives in the trees of the tropical rainforest.
48934.m: The toucan has a huge, colourful beak.

48935.q: Which fruit grows in the tropics?
48935.e: Bananas need lots of warmth and rain. That is why they grow in the tropics and not outdoors here.
48935.m: Bananas grow in warm tropical countries.

48936.q: Where does the cocoa for our chocolate grow?
48936.e: The cacao tree needs warmth all year and lots of rain. Switzerland buys its cocoa beans from tropical countries.
48936.m: Cocoa for Swiss chocolate comes from the tropics.

48937.q: Which drink comes from a plant that grows in the tropics?
48937.e: Coffee bushes grow in warm tropical countries, for example in Brazil. Their roasted beans make coffee.

48938.q: About how many hours of daylight are there in the tropics each day?
48938.e: In the tropics, day and night are about the same length all year. It is light there for about 12 hours every day.
48938.m: In the tropics it is light for about 12 hours every day.

a: A mountain of snow on land
48939.e: An iceberg is a large piece of ice that has broken off a glacier. Most of it lies hidden under the water.
48939.m: Most of an iceberg lies under water.

48940.q: What is the chart called that shows the temperature and precipitation of a place over the year?
48940.e: A climate graph shows the average temperature and precipitation for each month. This makes it easy to compare places.
48940.m: A climate graph shows the temperature and precipitation of a place.

48941.q: What are the Earth’s two polar regions called?
48941.e: The Arctic lies around the North Pole, the Antarctic around the South Pole. It is very cold in both regions.
48941.m: The two polar regions are the Arctic and the Antarctic.

48942.q: What can easily start in the dry grass during the dry season?
48942.e: Dry grass burns very easily. That is why there are often bush fires in the dry season.
48942.m: Dry grass can catch fire easily.

48943.q: What often happens in the afternoon during the rainy season in the tropics?
48943.e: In the morning the sun heats the damp air a lot. In the afternoon tall clouds often form with violent thunderstorms.
48943.m: In the rainy season there are often thunderstorms in the afternoon.

48944.q: What lies under the ice at the North Pole?
48944.e: There is no land at the North Pole. The ice there floats on the Arctic Ocean.
48944.m: At the North Pole the ice floats on the sea.

48945.q: What happens to the sun in winter in the polar regions?
a: It does not rise for a long time
48945.e: In winter the sun stays below the horizon there for weeks or months. This is called the polar night.
48945.m: In the polar night the sun does not rise for a long time.

48946.q: Which warm, dry wind often blows in Swiss Alpine valleys?
48946.e: The föhn comes down from the mountains into the valley and becomes warm and dry on the way. It is well known in the Reuss valley in Uri, for example.
48946.m: The föhn is a warm, dry wind in the Alps.

48947.q: What are the colourful lights in the night sky near the poles called?
48947.e: The northern and southern lights glow green, red or violet in the sky. You see them mainly in areas near the poles.
48947.m: The polar lights glow in colours in the night sky.

48948.q: Why is it so cold in the polar regions?
a: The sun is further away there
48948.e: In the polar regions the sun shines on the Earth at a very low angle. So its rays give only a little warmth.
48948.m: Sun rays at a low angle give only a little warmth.

48949.q: When do cherry trees blossom here?
48949.e: When it gets warmer in spring, the cherry trees blossom white. Then in summer you can pick the cherries.

48950.q: Which month is usually the coldest in Switzerland?
48950.e: On average, January is the coldest month in Switzerland. The days are still short then.
48950.m: January is usually our coldest month.

a: Between the tropics and the polar region
Only in the middle of the sea
48951.e: The temperate zone lies between the warm and the cold regions of the Earth. That is why it is sometimes warm and sometimes cold there.
48951.m: The temperate zone lies between warm and cold.

48952.q: What do many deciduous trees here do in autumn?
48952.e: In autumn the leaves turn colourful and fall off. That way the trees save water and energy in winter.
48952.m: Deciduous trees shed their leaves in autumn.

48953.q: Which tree is a typical deciduous tree in Switzerland?
48953.e: The beech is one of the most common deciduous trees in Switzerland. It grows in many forests on the Swiss Plateau.
48953.m: The beech is a common deciduous tree here.

48954.q: What weather do we often have in Switzerland in winter?
48954.e: In winter it gets cold here. It often freezes, and it can snow.
48954.m: In winter there is often frost and snow here.

48955.q: Which country lies in the temperate zone like Switzerland?
48955.e: Germany lies north of Switzerland and also has four seasons. The other countries lie on the equator.
48955.m: Germany is also in the temperate zone.

48956.e: The hedgehog finds hardly any food in winter. That is why it sleeps in a pile of leaves until spring.

48957.q: In which canton do even palm trees grow outdoors by the lakes?
48957.e: Ticino lies south of the Alps and has mild winters. That is why palm trees grow by Lake Maggiore and Lake Lugano.
48957.m: The climate in Ticino is especially mild.

a: Between the tropics and the temperate zone
In the middle of the polar region
48958.e: The subtropics border the tropics. They lie between the tropics and the temperate zone.
48958.m: The subtropics lie right next to the tropics.

48959.q: What are summers like by the Mediterranean?
48959.e: The Mediterranean lies in the subtropics. In summer it is hot there for a long time and it hardly rains.
48959.m: Summers by the Mediterranean are hot and dry.

48960.q: What are winters by the Mediterranean usually like?
48960.e: In winter it is mild by the Mediterranean. Most of the rain falls there at this time.
48960.m: By the Mediterranean it rains mainly in winter.

48961.q: Which fruit typically grows by the Mediterranean?
48961.e: Olive trees like hot, dry summers and mild winters. That is why they grow all around the Mediterranean.
48961.m: Olive trees grow all around the Mediterranean.

48962.q: From which country does Switzerland get many oranges in winter?
48962.e: Spain lies on the Mediterranean and has mild winters. Many oranges grow there, and some of them come to Switzerland.

48963.q: What is the large, hot desert in the north of Africa called?
48963.e: The Sahara lies in the north of Africa. It is very hot there, and it almost never rains.
48963.m: The Sahara is a large desert in Africa.

48964.q: Which animal lives in the Sahara?
48964.e: The dromedary has one hump and can go a long time without water. It is adapted to the hot desert.
48964.m: The dromedary can go a long time without water.

48965.q: Which plant stores water in its stem in hot, dry areas?
48965.e: The cactus has a thick stem in which it stores water. Its spines protect it from animals.
48965.m: Cacti store water in their thick stems.

48966.q: Why do many families like going to the Mediterranean in summer?
a: Because the sun often shines there
Because there is lots of snow there
Because it is often foggy there
Because it rains almost all the time there
48966.e: By the Mediterranean there are lots of sunny days in summer. That is why many people go there on holiday.
48966.m: The sun often shines by the Mediterranean.

48967.e: In the rainy season it rains often and heavily for several months. It happens mainly in warm countries.
48967.m: In the rainy season it rains a lot for several months.

48968.q: Where are there rainy and dry seasons instead of summer and winter?
a: In warm countries near the equator
48968.e: In many warm regions it stays warm all year. There the seasons are told apart by the rain.
48968.m: In warm countries people talk about a rainy season and a dry season.

48969.q: What happens to the rivers in the rainy season?
a: They carry a lot of water
48969.e: All the rain fills the rivers. Sometimes they even burst their banks.
48969.m: In the rainy season the rivers carry a lot of water.

48970.q: What does the grass look like in the rainy season?
48970.e: With the rain the grass grows quickly. The landscape turns green and the animals find plenty of food.
48970.m: In the rainy season the landscape turns green.

48971.q: When do the waterholes in Africa fill up again?
48971.e: When it rains a lot, the water collects in hollows and pools. That way the waterholes fill up again.
48971.m: The rain fills up the waterholes again.

48972.e: In the dry season hardly any rain falls for several months. The ground becomes hard and dusty.
48972.m: In the dry season it hardly rains for months.

48973.q: What does the grass look like in the dry season?
48973.e: Without rain the grass dries out. It turns yellow and brown.
48973.m: In the dry season the grass dries out.

48974.q: What happens to many waterholes in the dry season?
48974.e: Without rain the water evaporates in the heat. Many waterholes become small or dry up completely.
48974.m: Many waterholes dry up in the dry season.

48975.q: Why do many animals in Africa travel far in the dry season?
a: They are looking for water and grass
They are looking for cool caves
They are fleeing from the sea
48975.e: In the dry season food becomes scarce. That is why wildebeest and zebras move to where there is still water and grass.
48975.m: In the dry season many animals travel to water and grass.

48976.e: The monsoon is a huge wind. In summer it blows from a different direction than in winter.
48976.m: The monsoon is a wind that turns with the seasons.

48977.q: In which country is the monsoon especially well known?
48977.e: In India the monsoon brings the most important rain every year. Everyone waits for it in summer.
48977.m: The monsoon is very important in India.

48978.q: Why is the monsoon rain so important for India?
a: It brings sand to the beaches
48978.e: Many farmers in India have no other sources of water. Without the monsoon rain the harvest would dry up.
48978.m: Without monsoon rain the harvest in India would dry up.

48979.q: Where does the summer monsoon blow to India from?
48979.e: The summer monsoon comes from the Indian Ocean. That is why it is so damp.
48979.m: The summer monsoon comes from the sea.

48980.q: What is the weather in India usually like at the time of the winter monsoon?
48980.e: The winter monsoon blows from the land. This air is dry, so in most areas it rains little then.
48980.m: The winter monsoon usually brings dry weather.

48981.q: Which crop do many farmers in monsoon countries grow?
48981.e: Rice grows well in wet fields. All the monsoon rain helps farmers in Asia with this.
48981.m: Rice grows well in wet fields.

48982.q: What can very heavy monsoon rain cause?
48982.e: When too much rain falls at once, rivers burst their banks. Then roads and fields are under water.
48982.m: Too much monsoon rain can bring floods.

48983.q: In which months is the summer monsoon in India, roughly?
48983.e: The summer monsoon starts in India around June. It lasts until about September.
48983.m: The summer monsoon lasts from about June to September.

48984.q: What does the Arabic word that ‘monsoon’ comes from mean?
48984.e: The word monsoon comes from the Arabic word ‘mausim’. It means season, because the wind changes with the season.

a: What it is like outside right now
What it is like over many years
48985.e: The weather is what we experience outside today or tomorrow. It can change quickly.
48985.m: The weather is the state of the air right now.

48986.q: Is ‘It will rain in Bern tomorrow’ a statement about weather or climate?
48986.e: The statement is only about one day and one place. So it is about the weather.
48986.m: Statements about a single day are about the weather.

48987.q: What do you use to measure temperature?
48987.e: A thermometer shows how warm or cold it is. Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

48988.q: What do you use to measure how much rain has fallen?
48988.e: A rain gauge is a container that catches the rain. That way you can see how much water has fallen.
48988.m: A rain gauge catches the rain.

48989.q: What does a weather vane show?
48989.e: The weather vane turns with the wind. That way you can see where the wind is blowing from.
48989.m: A weather vane shows where the wind is blowing from.

48990.q: What is the name of Switzerland’s weather service, which makes the weather forecast?
48990.e: MeteoSwiss forecasts the weather for the whole of Switzerland. It also warns of thunderstorms and storms.

48991.e: For climate, you look at what the weather in a place is usually like. You need measurements from many years for that.
48991.m: Climate is the typical weather over many years.

48992.q: Over how many years is climate usually worked out?
48992.e: Experts usually take the weather data from 30 years. From that they work out what the weather in a place is normally like.
48992.m: For climate, you usually look at 30 years.

48993.q: Is ‘It is almost always dry in the Sahara’ a statement about weather or climate?
48993.e: The statement describes what it is normally like there over many years. So it is about the climate.
48993.m: What is normal for a place is part of its climate.

48994.q: What do you call the large areas of the Earth with a similar climate?
48994.e: The Earth is divided into climate zones. In each climate zone the climate is similar.
48994.m: Areas with a similar climate are called climate zones.

a: In the middle of the Sahara
48995.e: The tundra lies in the far north, right next to the permanent ice. It is cold there most of the time.
48995.m: The tundra lies near the polar region.

48996.q: Which plants grow in the tundra?
48996.e: In the tundra mainly low plants grow, such as mosses, lichens and dwarf shrubs. They stay low to escape the wind and cold.
48996.m: Mosses and lichens grow in the tundra.

48997.q: Why do almost no trees grow in the tundra?
48997.e: Trees need enough warmth to grow. In the tundra it is too cold for that almost all year.
48997.m: It is too cold for trees in the tundra.

48998.q: Which animal moves through the tundra in large herds?
48998.e: Reindeer eat lichens and mosses. In summer and winter they roam about in large herds.
48998.m: Reindeer live in large herds in the tundra.

48999.q: What do you call ground that stays frozen all year?
48999.e: In the tundra the ground only thaws a little at the top. Below that it always stays frozen; this is called permafrost.
48999.m: Permafrost is ground that always stays frozen.

49000.q: What is summer like in the tundra?
49000.e: Summer in the tundra lasts only a few weeks. Even then it does not get really warm.
49000.m: The tundra summer is short and cool.

49001.q: Which small rodent of the tundra is known for its migrations?
49001.e: The lemming is a small rodent from the far north. When there are very many of them, they travel far and wide.
49001.m: Lemmings are small rodents of the tundra.

49002.q: Where in Switzerland is there a landscape similar to the tundra?
49002.e: Above the tree line in the Alps, only low plants grow. This is similar to the tundra in the far north.
49002.m: High in the Alps there is a kind of tundra.

49003.q: What mainly grows in the savannah?
49003.e: The savannah is a wide grassland. Single trees and bushes stand here and there.
49003.m: Grass with scattered trees grows in the savannah.

49004.q: On which continent are there large savannahs with lions?
49004.e: Large parts of Africa are savannah. Lions live there in prides.

49005.q: Which animal with a very long neck eats leaves from trees in the savannah?
49005.e: The giraffe is the tallest animal in the world. With its long neck it reaches leaves high up in the trees.
49005.m: The giraffe is the tallest animal in the world.

49006.q: Which black-and-white striped animal lives in the savannah?
49006.e: The zebra has black and white stripes. Every zebra has its own stripe pattern.
49006.m: Every zebra has its own stripe pattern.

49007.q: Which thick tree is typical of the African savannah?
49007.e: The baobab, also called the monkey-bread tree, has a very thick trunk. It stores water in it.
49007.m: The baobab stores water in its thick trunk.

49008.q: Which land animal of the savannah is the largest in the world?
49008.e: The African elephant is the largest and heaviest land animal. It lives in herds in the savannah.
49008.m: The African elephant is the largest land animal.

49009.q: Which animal of the savannah is the fastest land animal?
49009.e: For a short time the cheetah can run at more than 90 kilometres per hour. That is how it hunts fast antelopes.
49009.m: The cheetah is the fastest land animal.

49010.q: What is the name of a famous national park with savannah in Tanzania?
49010.e: The Serengeti lies in Tanzania in East Africa. Huge herds of wildebeest and zebras live there.
49010.m: The Serengeti is a famous savannah in Tanzania.

a: In the middle of the taiga
49011.e: The savannah is drier than the rainforest but wetter than the desert. That is why it lies between the two.
49011.m: The savannah lies between rainforest and desert.

a: Wide grassland with almost no trees
49012.e: The steppe is a wide, flat grassland. Hardly any trees grow there.

49013.q: Why do hardly any trees grow in the steppe?
a: The ground is made of ice
49013.e: In the steppe too little rain falls for trees. Grasses can manage with less water.
49013.m: In the steppe there is too little rain for trees.

49014.q: What are winters like in the steppes of Asia?
49014.e: The steppes of Asia lie far from the sea. That is why the winters there are very cold and the summers hot.
49014.m: The steppes of Asia have very cold winters.

49015.q: In which country do many nomads travel through the steppe with their herds?
49015.e: Mongolia has huge steppes. Many families there move with their animals from pasture to pasture.
49015.m: Many nomads live in the steppe in Mongolia.

49016.e: A yurt is a round tent made of wood and felt. Nomads can take it down and bring it with them.
49016.m: A yurt is a round tent used by nomads.

49017.q: Which animals do nomads in the Mongolian steppe often keep?
49017.e: Horses are very important for the nomads in Mongolia. They ride them and use them to herd their animals.
49017.m: Horses are very important in Mongolia.

49018.q: What is the steppe in North America called?
49018.e: The steppe in North America is called the prairie. Huge herds of bison used to live there.
49018.m: The steppe in North America is called the prairie.

49019.q: What is the steppe in Argentina called?
49019.e: The steppe in Argentina is called the pampas. Today many cattle graze there.
49019.m: The steppe in Argentina is called the pampas.

49020.q: Which grain is grown on many steppe soils today?
49020.e: Steppe soils are often very fertile. That is why a lot of wheat is grown there.
49020.m: A lot of wheat grows on steppe soils.

49021.q: What kind of forest is the taiga?
49021.e: The taiga is a huge coniferous forest in the cold north of the Earth. It is the largest forest area in the world.
49021.m: The taiga is a huge coniferous forest.

49022.q: The taiga is a huge forest in the cold north. Which trees mainly grow there?
49022.e: In the taiga mainly conifers grow, such as spruces, pines and larches. They cope well with the cold.
49022.m: Mainly conifers grow in the taiga.

49023.q: In which country is most of the taiga?
49023.e: Russia is the largest country on Earth. A large part of it is covered with taiga.
49023.m: Most of the taiga is in Russia.

49024.q: Which country in North America also has a lot of taiga?
49024.e: Canada lies far to the north. Large parts of the country are covered with coniferous forest.
49024.m: Canada also has a lot of taiga.

49025.q: Which large animal with broad antlers lives in the huge coniferous forest of the cold north?
49025.e: The elk, called moose in North America, is the largest deer in the world. The males have broad, shovel-shaped antlers.
49025.m: The elk is the largest deer in the world.

49026.q: Which predator lives in the huge coniferous forest of the cold north?
49026.e: The brown bear lives in the coniferous forests of the north. In winter it rests in a den.
49026.m: The brown bear lives in the coniferous forest of the north.

49027.q: The taiga is a huge forest in the far north. What are the winters like there?
49027.e: Winter in the taiga lasts many months. It can freeze very hard there.
49027.m: In the taiga the winters are long and cold.

49028.q: Which landscape lies north of the taiga?
49028.e: Where it gets even colder, the forests of the taiga stop. Further north the treeless tundra begins.
49028.m: The tundra lies north of the taiga.

49029.q: Which conifer of the taiga loses its needles in autumn?
49029.e: The larch is a special conifer. In autumn its needles turn yellow and fall off, here in the Alps too.
49029.m: The larch sheds its needles in autumn.

49030.q: What is the area around the North Pole called?
49030.e: The area around the North Pole is called the Arctic. It is cold there all year round.
49030.m: The Arctic is in the very north of the Earth.

49031.q: What lies in the middle of the Arctic?
49031.e: In the middle of the Arctic there is no land, but a sea. It is often covered with ice.
49031.m: In the middle of the Arctic there is a frozen sea.

49032.q: Which large island lies in the Arctic?
49032.e: Greenland is the largest island in the world and lies largely in the Arctic. It is almost completely covered with ice.
49032.m: Greenland is a huge island full of ice in the far north.

49033.q: What is it called when the sun shines at night too in the Arctic summer?
49033.e: In summer the sun does not set in the Arctic for weeks. This is called the midnight sun.
49033.m: With the midnight sun it stays light at night too.

49034.q: What is the time in winter called when the sun does not rise at all in the Arctic?
49034.e: In winter the sun stays below the horizon in the Arctic for weeks. This dark time is called the polar night.
49034.m: In the polar night it stays dark during the day too.

49035.q: Which fox lives in the Arctic and has white fur in winter?
49035.e: The Arctic fox has white fur in winter. That way it is well camouflaged in the snow.
49035.m: The Arctic fox has white fur in winter.

49036.q: Which deer with big antlers live in the far north and pull Father Christmas’s sleigh in stories?
49036.e: Reindeer live in the cold regions of the north. With them, the females have antlers too.
49036.m: Reindeer live in the far north and have antlers.

49037.q: Which country has a part in the Arctic?
49037.e: The north of Norway lies in the Arctic. Russia, Canada, the USA with Alaska and Denmark with Greenland also have areas there.
49037.m: Norway reaches far up into the Arctic.

49038.q: About how thick is the sea ice at the North Pole?
